chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who doubts in Allah and in His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), then he is a disbeliever.
ai.seo_question: What constitutes disbelief (kufr) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores that doubt (shakk) in the core tenets of Tawhid and Nubuwwah elevates one to the status of a kafir, reflecting the principle that faith requires firm conviction rather than mere nominal adherence. Scholars often contrast this with doubt in secondary matters, emphasizing that uncertainty in the divine messenger's authority strikes at the root of Islamic creed. This establishes a direct link between theological certainty and the validity of one's religious identity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who doubts in Allahazwj and in Hisazwj Rasoolsaww, so his is an Unbeliver (Kafir)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Whoever doubts Allah and the Messenger of Allah is an unbeliever.’”
